risks.title: Difficulty predicting and managing medical costs
risks.score_rationale: This risk is central in the 10-K, mentioned in the opening lines of Item 1A, with strong language ('material adverse effect'). The gap between projected and actual costs can directly impact profitability. The Industrial category is highly weighted here.

risks.title: Increased competition on pricing and margins
risks.score_rationale: The filing highlights pressure on pricing and margins, particularly in the pharmacy sector. The language is repeated and emphasizes a 'material adverse' impact. Competition is a core operational risk.

risks.title: Dependence on pharmaceutical price benchmarks
risks.score_rationale: The risk is clearly outlined with specific references to third-party benchmarks and the impact of laws such as the Inflation Reduction Act. The tone is concerned but less central than industrial risks.

risks.title: Loss of relationships with pharmaceutical manufacturers
risks.score_rationale: The risk is well-documented, with mention of non-exclusive contracts and potentially 'material adverse' impact. It is linked to increasing regulatory uncertainties.

risks.title: Changes in pharmacy networks
risks.score_rationale: The filing notes the importance of major pharmacy networks (47% of retail locations) and the risk of contract termination. The language is concerned, with reference to a 'material adverse' impact.

risks.title: Inaccuracy of medical care reserves
risks.score_rationale: The risk is described as inherent, uncertain, and sensitive to numerous factors. The text emphasizes direct impact on results if estimates are exceeded, using strong language.

risks.title: Regulatory pressure on premiums and fees
risks.score_rationale: The text explicitly mentions restrictions by federal and state agencies on premium increases. The risk is recurring and tied to government programs, affecting pricing flexibility.
